reference.source: Paley, Manual of Gothic Mouldings 1845, Plate I fig 6 (leaf n88)
reference.source_frame: plate pixels, y-down, on the 1930x2951 scan; anchor station wall_start = plate (1004, 772)
reference.notes: crop placement is ESTIMATED by eye from the overlay image; refine against the first render if the plane misregisters. Plate skew +0.1 deg (noise floor), uncorrected.

construction_plane.profile_x: +X = Paley's wall-line direction (horizontal, bottom of page)
construction_plane.profile_y: +Z = up the soffit direction, away from the wall-line

wall_start.note: origin: left end of the wall-line run

wall_end.note: wall-line meets the 44.2 deg arris chamfer

arris.note: arris cusp = bowtell arc start at a0 = -167.2 deg on the fitted circle; the 0.056 in gap the old chain carried here is closed by pinning the station to the fit

bead_exit.note: bowtell arc end at a1 = 100 deg; external tangency point of bowtell and hollow circles - a true cusp, the outline reverses here

hollow_end.note: intersection of the measured chamfer line with the constructed hollow circle, 0.021 in from the measured point - the measured triple (hollow construction, chamfer start, chamfer angle) is mutually inconsistent by that much and the closed outline forces the choice; source_px registers within tolerance

chamfer_top.note: moulding's top reach, on the stock right edge (soffit plane)

stock_top_right.note: 1.09 in of stock left uncut above the chamfer (recorded); height derived from measured scale, not printed

stock_bottom_left.note: stock left edge at plate x=1001, slightly left of the wall-line start

segments.name: wall_line
segments.note: the saw passed here - part of the traversal but not moulded edge

segments.name: arris_chamfer
segments.note: 44.2 deg measured; cycles 23-24 misidentified this member as a hollow

segments.name: bowtell
segments.note: least-squares fitted, residual mean 0.37 px; sweeps 267 deg through the soffit baseline (bottom) and the stock edge (right flank)

segments.name: bead_hollow
segments.note: the cavetto member. Centre by compass construction: on the bowtell's exit radial, r_hollow beyond - the circles are externally tangent at bead_exit. Old workflow's sweep=0.464 stopped 0.24 in short of the measured chamfer start; this arc runs to the geometrically consistent end (190.8 deg)

segments.name: soffit_uncut
segments.note: the uncut 1.09 in of stock above the chamfer, along the soffit plane

stock_width.note: printed '11 in' on the plate; 10.91 measured, 0.8% off print

stock_height.note: derived from measured scale - NOT printed

wall_angle.note: measured, not assumed level - 4 px over 100 at the engraving's noise floor

notes: PILOT PROFILE - the corrected cavetto (fig 6 carries the cavetto as its bead_hollow member).

Closure decision: the stock rectangle closes the outline, per the recorded cycle-27 format decision ('members should NOT close the loop; the block's bounding planes close it'). The measured upper-face line at plate y~722 (cycles 26-27) is real but its routing into the outline is an OPEN QUESTION - it is deliberately not asserted here. Refining it later changes only the upper-left bounding region, never the moulded edge.

Old-workflow defects this spec corrects: (1) the heading-chained hollow stopped 0.24 in short of the measured chamfer start; (2) the old chain's final point landed at x=11.007, poking 0.23 in through the soffit plane; (3) a 0.056 in break at the arris between chamfer end and fitted arc start; (4) the old roll exit-heading convention disagreed with its own sampled arc direction by 180 deg and the hollow was chained off the wrong heading - compensated invisibly.

Both arcs are COUNTERCLOCKWISE in the y-up profile frame. The bowtell/hollow circles are externally tangent at bead_exit (2.83 = 2.29 + 0.54): the joins at bead_exit and hollow_end are true cusps, declared HARD.
No SMOOTH join exists in this profile; the ogee stress profile exercises that vocabulary.
